articles.title: Shift in pension and insurance money to equities dampens long-term G-sec demand: RBI DG
articles.content: The demand for long-term government securities has seen a marginal decline recently. Insurance companies and pension funds are increasingly focusing on equities instead of sovereign debt. This change has impacted the stability of the government securities market and highlighted challenges in liquidity distribution. The Reserve Bank of India emphasizes the need for a coordinated approach and broader participation from institutional investors.

articles.title: A 50 bps jumbo rate hike can lead to financial stability concerns, hurt growth: Report
articles.content: SBI economists have lowered their rate hike expectations for the upcoming RBI policy review. They now anticipate a 0.25 per cent increase rather than the previously expected 0.50 per cent. This adjustment stems from concerns regarding financial stability and potential impacts on economic growth. The RBI's monetary policy committee is scheduled to meet from December 2 to December 4.

articles.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sells shares worth USD 280.41 million following IPO
articles.content: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, sold shares worth USD 280.41 million after the company's IPO. He reported holding 202.8 million shares and additional shares through trusts. Despite the decline, shares remained above their initial offering price of USD 83.

articles.title: RBI DG asks primary dealers to bid responsibly in G-Sec underwriting auctions
articles.content: RBI Deputy Governor Rohit Jain has urged primary dealers to bid responsibly in government securities auctions. Jain noted instances of volatile pricing that misalign with orderly market conditions, impacting government borrowing costs. He highlighted the challenge of liquidity concentration in a few securities and called for improved market-making activities. Jain also pointed out declining demand from institutional investors for long-term sovereign debt amid uncertain interest rates.

articles.title: IIFCL IPO: Govt plans to sell part of its stake, company to issue fresh shares
articles.content: The government aims to partially divest its shareholding in India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd through an initial public offering. The IPO is expected to occur by the end of the current fiscal year, according to an official statement. IIFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital alongside the government stake sale. The proceeds from the stake sale will contribute to the government's disinvestment revenue.

articles.content: In a remarkable surge this month, Indian equity markets have observed a substantial upswing, with the BSE Sensex climbing nearly 11 percent. Motivated by lower crude oil prices and impressive Q2 earnings, investor optimism soared, although a recent profit booking saw a minor dip of nearly 2 percent.

articles.title: The LTCG debate: Why markets need tax stability and not ad-hoc fixes
articles.content: Foreign Institutional Investor capital is leaving Indian markets, raising concerns over the unpredictability of tax policies. Investors are urging for the reconsideration of Long-Term Capital Gains tax provisions. Historical changes in LTCG have created volatility that affects long-term investors negatively. A stable tax policy framework is essential to attract and retain investment in the Indian financial market.

articles.title: Bitcoin fails to hold Nvidia bump with crypto headwinds in focus
articles.content: Bitcoin's recent 1% decline has overshadowed positive developments from Nvidia, leading to a dip in investor confidence. The fallout from the Binance hack and notable ETF outflows has further complicated the situation. With the Federal Reserve's potential rate hikes looming in December, many investors are hesitant, preferring to wait for clearer recovery signals despite attractive buying opportunities at current levels, erasing much of Bitcoin's value since its October 2025 peak.

articles.title: South Korea’s Kospi rockets 8% as AI-linked stocks get breather after Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. Worst over?
articles.content: South Korean shares have bounced back sharply after previously hitting a ten-month low, with the KOSPI index climbing 7.19%. This surge was largely driven by a rebound in technology stocks, particularly following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return to leadership. Notable AI companies such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix recorded substantial gains, while foreign investments showed a positive trend with net purchases totaling 497.3 billion won.

articles.title: India’s rupee has become an accidental carry star
articles.content: The Reserve Bank of India has made moves that temporarily attract carry traders to the rupee. Recent factors include decreasing oil prices and a shift in foreign investment from artificial intelligence stocks to Indian markets. However, these RBI incentives may not last, leaving uncertainty for traders. India's interest rate advantage has significantly diminished since 2011, raising concerns. Policymakers face challenges in ensuring sustained interest in the rupee amid historical depreciation.

articles.content: US stocks rebounded sharply on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive following pressure from President Donald Trump, reversing part of last week’s tech-led market rout. This settlement received the green light from the Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal, buoyed by considerable backing from claimants.

articles.title: Rupee retreats with stocks as rally takes a breather, positive bias lingers
articles.content: After a five-day rise, the Indian rupee faced a setback on Monday, driven by heightened dollar demand from major corporations. This shift in momentum was compounded by profit-taking activities. The rupee settled at 92.91 against the dollar, following a peak of 92.44. Additionally, underwhelming local stock performance fueled a bearish outlook for the rupee. Nevertheless, analysts predict a sustained positive sentiment towards stocks and currencies amid ongoing evaluations.

articles.content: Germany's government bond yields increased marginally on Monday as equity markets began to rebound, leading to diminished interest in safe-haven assets. articles.title: Rupee retreats, Goldman calls it a 'port of stability' in AI storm
articles.content: The Indian rupee initially rose to a seven-month high before retreating amid corporate dollar buying. It is on track for a monthly gain of over 2%, bolstered by significant foreign investment in Indian equities. Analysts noted that the rupee's early gains pushed it into overbought territory, prompting some selling. Despite recent fluctuations, the rupee has remained stable compared to other major currencies.
